verdict.note: YATU Chromium proof on clean committed tree: Explorer open → closed → Sessions open; reload preserved Sessions projection, hash stayed unchanged, and dock-modebar count was zero.

real Chromium, sampled in-page across rAF frames. Context dock opening: frame at t=10ms width 1px with animationName dock-in, settling at 276px over 27 samples; closing: still mounted with .dock-closing and dock-out at t~60ms, gone after one duration. Sessions forest: same dock-out class and unmount via the rail panel control. Left dock unchanged, now on the same useFold. .ctx-body scroller present, so the clipped fold cannot hide a long list.

Real Chromium 1440x900, sampled per animation frame in-page. BEFORE (same probe expression, measured on the tree without this change): band width 1..204 across sessions to spec and again spec to sessions — it collapsed to a pixel and grew back. AFTER: 204..204 flat in both directions, the band never dips; the only movement left is the 6px slide the dissolve is made of (document seam 238..244). The probe was corrected first: it had been reading .app-main, a different element on each route, and reported a 204px lurch that was entirely its own confusion.

Re-measured on the shell dock and the Sessions forest, sampled per animation frame from inside the page. Closing keeps the element mounted for 10 (dock) / 7 (forest) frames carrying .dock-closing and running dock-out, width shrinking to 5.0 / 8.9px, then unmounted after one --dur-panel. Opening runs dock-in from a 1px minimum up to the settled width. Both settle at 204 — one region, one number. No fourth animation name (dock-in / dock-out / dock-swap only). RECORDED because it cost me two wrong runs: useFold sets `closing` in an EFFECT, so between open=false and closing=true there is a single render where the element is unmounted — a probe that breaks on the first null misses the entire closing phase and reports it as 'no closing at all'. The marker is also the CLASS .dock-closing, not a data attribute. Neither is a defect; both are things a re-measurement has to know.

Re-measured across Sessions to spec and back, sampling the band's RIGHT EDGE per frame from inside the page and taking whichever component is actually PAINTING it (width > 0). Both components draw it across the run, the edge is the same number before and after, and it never collapses. My first probe took the first matching selector and read a zero-width unmounting sibling — it reported a 244px dip, which is exactly the invented lurch this scenario's description warns about, so the warning earned its place twice.

RE-ANCHORED on the synced tree (main had moved 36 commits and folded packages/terminal-ui into spec-dashboard/src/terminal, touching styles.css among others). Re-driven through the real product; result unchanged. Both bands: closing stays mounted carrying .dock-closing under dock-out and unmounts after one --dur-panel; opening runs dock-in from a 1px minimum; both settle at 204 — one region, one number.

RE-ANCHORED on the synced tree (main had moved 36 commits and folded packages/terminal-ui into spec-dashboard/src/terminal, touching styles.css among others). Re-driven through the real product; result unchanged. Right edge sampled per frame from whichever component is actually painting it: same number before and after, never collapses.

Measured against the PRE-FIX source (66cc806b0's useFold.js/styles.css/Dock.jsx/Shell.jsx/SessionInterface.jsx/SessionForestPanel.jsx/ContextDock.jsx checked into the running tree), so the stamped codeSha is the repair commit, not the tree measured. One click to OPEN produced THREE distinct animation stretches: dock-swap on the un-flagged mount frame, then dock-in, then dock-swap again when the fold flag dropped and CSS's unconditional handover rule took over. Width also reached its full 204px at 59ms of a 170ms open while opacity was still 0.00 — the keyframe was running max-width to the 640px cap, a distance the band does not travel. 1/2 folds were a single movement.

Same probe, same four gestures, on the committed tree. Every gesture is now exactly ONE animation stretch: fold open dock-in only, fold close dock-out only, and dock-swap in BOTH handover directions at a flat 204px — sessions→spec had no dissolve at all before, because the shell's fold state never sees the route switch that replaces its own dock. Width now reaches 204px at 226ms of the open with opacity 1.00 rather than at 59ms with opacity 0.00: the keyframe animates the band's own width, so the fade and the slide describe the same gesture. 2/2 folds a single movement.

Re-measured after the fold was rewritten to animate the band's own width. All three panels sampled per animation frame from inside the page. Opening: each carries data-fold=in and runs dock-in ALONE — one animation, not the two the boolean flag used to produce — from 1px up to its settled width (dock 204, context dock 276, forest 204). Closing: each stays mounted 8 / 9 / 6 frames carrying .dock-closing under dock-out, width down to 1-2px, then unmounted; at ~16.6ms a frame that is one --dur-panel. Same two names, same duration, three panels. .ctx-body scroller present, so the clipped fold still cannot hide a long list. The context dock is newly ON this mechanism rather than beside it: it had no data-fold at all before, so it was the one panel that popped open with no arrival animation while both left bands slid.

Same run, band right edge sampled per frame from whichever component paints it. Width is 204 flat across every switch in both directions — the band never dips, so the fold is not being run for something that was never a fold. dock-swap runs in BOTH directions now (right edge 238..244, the 6px slide the dissolve is made of); before this commit sessions→spec had no dissolve at all, because the shell stays mounted across that switch so its own fold state never saw it. A THIRD row in the transcript records a case this scenario had not distinguished: on a REVISIT to a route whose pane is already in the view pool, nothing remounts, so no dissolve runs at all (right edge a flat 244, animations none). The width guarantee still holds, and this is not new — the old unconditional rule also only fired on mount — but the dissolve is a first-visit effect, not a per-switch one.

Third reading of this scenario, and the one that matters for the deployment: measured on the LIVE gateway at :9443 after the merge landed, not on a dev server. Signed in through the gateway's own login form. Confirmed the page is a BUILT bundle with no vite client, and fetched the served stylesheet back out of the browser to confirm it contains [data-fold=swap] — the fix is in the bytes the gateway hands a human, not just in the repo. Then drove the rail fold control: close is one dock-out stretch, open is one dock-in stretch, 2/2 gestures a single movement, band settling at 204px. This is the step a frontend merge does not get for free — the backend hot-reloads but the gateway serves a prebuilt dist, so a merged frontend change is invisible until that dist is rebuilt.
